objections.text: The hand-derived duplicate-key case sends the same first and second rego values and already requires OPENJSON-compatible first-occurrence behavior. A02 repeats that input and mechanism.
objections.resolution: A02 now duplicates the numeric temp key rather than rego, and makes the second occurrence exponent notation that would fail if selected. It tests first-occurrence handling through a distinct typed conversion path.

objections.text: The hand-derived temperature-rounding case already sends temp 3.965 in the same document shape and requires 3.97. A03 is the same attack with only the registration changed.
objections.resolution: A03 now sends -3.965. The negative midpoint distinguishes half-away-from-zero (-3.97) from half-up and half-even (-3.96), unlike the positive hand-derived midpoint.

objections.text: The hand-derived NULL-document case already calls the procedure with a NULL argument and requires no error and no inserted rows. A06 is identical.
objections.resolution: A06 now sends the JSON scalar text 'null', not SQL NULL. SQL Server ISJSON without a type constraint rejects that scalar, exposing a conversion that accepts all JSON values.
